summary.intent: Add Phase 27 (Writable Shares PoC) to the roadmap and capture implementation decisions via the discuss-phase workflow, building on Phase 14's read-only sharing infrastructure.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 was added to the roadmap with a cleaned-up slug, STATE.md updated, and a full CONTEXT.md was written capturing decisions across four gray areas: IPNS key delivery, write scope, share dialog changes, and conflict/attribution.

repo: CipherBox sidesteps the general 'unsolved multi-writer IPNS' problem because all IPNS publishes go through the API server, which acts as a coordination point — the PITFALLS.md doc explicitly states this.

The existing optimistic concurrency system (expectedSequenceNumber + 409 conflict detection) already handles multi-writer scenarios identically to multi-device sync — the server checks sequence numbers regardless of which user publishes.

Phase 14 deferred writable shares explicitly: read-write sharing requires giving recipients the IPNS signing key, and multi-writer IPNS was labeled 'unsolved' — but the server-relayed architecture resolves this without protocol-level changes.
Milestone 4 (TEAM-11) plans a cryptographic read/write key hierarchy so viewers literally cannot write — Phase 27 PoC precedes this and may need alignment with that future design.
share_keys table already exists from Phase 14; Phase 27 extends it with a permission level field (read-only vs read-write).

code.finding: expectedSequenceNumber is checked server-side before every IPNS publish — works regardless of which user submits, making multi-writer coordination already functional.
Sequence comparison logic: network vs DB cache, highest wins — handles concurrent publisher scenarios.
409 Conflict detection with automatic single-retry + re-sync — the same flow that would handle two write-share recipients colliding.
UI conflict banner with jitter-delayed retry — already built for multi-device, reusable for multi-writer share conflicts.

workflow: The gsd-tools CLI generates slugs from full phase descriptions, which can produce absurdly long directory names — manual slug cleanup was needed after add-phase ran.
The depends-on field in the roadmap entry defaulted to the previous phase (26) rather than the logically correct dependency (Phase 14) — required manual correction.

discuss-phase workflow structured four gray areas: IPNS key delivery, write scope for recipients, share dialog changes, and conflict/attribution — all explored interactively before writing CONTEXT.md.

friction: gsd-tools generated an excessively long slug from the full phase description; required manual directory rename and roadmap entry correction.
Roadmap 'Depends on' was auto-set to Phase 26 (sequential neighbor) rather than Phase 14 (the actual logical dependency) — required a manual edit.
STATE.md needed multiple read/edit cycles to find and update the Roadmap Evolution section correctly.
open_items: IPNS signing key delivery via metadata embedding (in IPNS record itself) is deferred to a future decentralization phase — current PoC wraps key alongside folderKey via ECIES.
Milestone 4 TEAM-11 cryptographic read/write key hierarchy needs to be reconciled with Phase 27's PoC approach before M4 planning.
Multi-writer CRDTs for IPNS (requiring all writers to have the IPNS private key for folder metadata) noted as a future consideration once write-sharing is established.
Re-sharing permissions (whether read-write recipients can share further) deferred — Phase 27 PoC does not address re-sharing.
Attribution/audit trail for writes by share recipients deferred beyond PoC scope.
